title: Sigma/pi, hybridisation and resonance; formal charge; Stereoisomerism (E/Z and optical)
specRef: C3.2(b), C3.2(d), C3.2(e), OA1.2(a) and others; C3.2(f), OA1.1(a), OA1.1(b), OA1.1(c) and others
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: BD07#t3 term and clue written for the game; OR05#t2 term and clue written for the game; BD07#t4 term and clue written for the game; OR05#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: BD07#N.5, OR05#N.4a, BD07#N.13, OR05#N.5, OR05#N.8, OR05#N.12, OR05#N.14c.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Free rotation
items.clue: Groups can turn about a single C–C link, but not about C=C.

items.label: Pi bond
items.clue: Sideways overlap of p orbitals, above and below the plane of a C=C.

items.label: Trigonal planar
items.clue: Arrangement around each C of C=C: three bonding regions at about 120°.

items.label: Stereoisomers
items.clue: Compounds with one structural formula but different arrangements of atoms in space.

questions.stem: A student suggests that a π bond between two carbon atoms prevents rotation about the bond that joins them. Which observation does this hypothesis predict?

options.text: ClHC=CHCl exists as two separable compounds
ClH₂C–CH₂Cl exists as two separable compounds
H₂C=CHCl exists as two separable compounds
ClC≡CCl exists as two separable compounds

questions.explanation: With no rotation, the two Cl atoms are fixed on the same side or opposite sides of C=C: two isomers. ClH₂C–CH₂Cl has no π bond, so it rotates and is one compound.

questions.stem: In one stereoisomer of 2-chlorobut-2-ene, CH₃CCl=CHCH₃, the Cl atom and the H atom are on the same side of the C=C. Which is correct?

options.text: It is Z, because the Cl atom and the H atom are on the same side.
It is E, because the priority groups, Cl and CH₃, are on opposite sides.
It is Z, because the two CH₃ groups are on the same side.
It has no E/Z isomers, because one of its C=C carbons carries a CH₃ group.

questions.explanation: C2: Cl outranks CH₃. C3: CH₃ outranks H. Cl is on the H side, so it is opposite the CH₃ on C3: E.

questions.stem: Mean (average) bond enthalpies: C–C 347 kJ mol⁻¹ · C=C 612 kJ mol⁻¹ · C≡C 838 kJ mol⁻¹. A C≡C bond is only about 2.4 times as strong as a C–C bond, not 3 times. Which statement explains this?

options.text: Its three shared pairs repel one another, so C≡C is longer than C–C.
All three of its bonds are σ bonds, but they are weaker because they share space.
Two of its three bonds come from sideways overlap of p orbitals, which is less effective.
Its π electrons lie on the axis between the nuclei, where σ electrons repel them.

questions.explanation: C≡C is one σ and two π. Each π adds less than a σ: 612 − 347 = 265, then 838 − 612 = 226. So the total is well below 3 × 347 = 1041.

questions.stem: Which compound can exist as E and Z stereoisomers about its C=C bond?

options.text: CH₂=C(CH₃)₂
CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃
CCl₂=CHCl
CH₃CH₂CH=CHCH₂CH₃

questions.explanation: Each C=C carbon carries an H and a C₂H₅. Rotation is blocked, so the two arrangements are different compounds.

questions.stem: Which carbon atom in 3-methylhexane, CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₂CH₃, is a chiral centre?

options.text: C2
C4
C3
None, as every group on C3 starts with a carbon atom.

questions.explanation: C3 carries H, CH₃, C₂H₅ and CH₂CH₂CH₃: four different groups.

questions.stem: 2-Hydroxypropanoic acid made in the laboratory from non-chiral starting materials is a racemic mixture. Which statement about this sample is correct?

options.text: Its molecules are achiral, which is why it does not rotate plane-polarised light.
It holds equal amounts of both enantiomers, whose rotations cancel.
It contains equal amounts of the E and Z isomers.
Fractional distillation separates it into its two enantiomers.

questions.explanation: Each enantiomer rotates the plane by the same angle in opposite directions. In a 1 : 1 mixture the effects cancel.

questions.stem: Butan-2-ol, CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃, exists as two stereoisomers with identical boiling points. Which explains why there are two?

options.text: Rotation about the C2–C3 bond is restricted, so the molecule has E and Z isomers.
C2 has four different groups, so the molecule cannot be superimposed on its mirror image.
The –OH group can be on C1 or on C2 of the chain, so there are two position isomers of it.
Every molecule has a mirror image, so every organic compound exists as two stereoisomers.

questions.explanation: C2 carries H, OH, CH₃ and C₂H₅: a chiral centre. The two stereoisomers are enantiomers.
